We measured extractable fluorinated compounds in textile samples at four stages of simulated use: new, after 10 abrasion cycles, after 50 cycles, and after 20 wash cycles. Samples were extracted with methanol in an ultrasonic bath and analyzed by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry, with isotope-labeled internal standards used for quantification. Measured concentrations rose in the early abrasion stages, likely due to fiber breakdown exposing previously inaccessible compounds, then declined as material was lost from the surface. Washing reduced concentrations by 40 to 70 percent depending on compound class. Method detection limits ranged from 0.05 to 0.4 ng/g. Because levels changed substantially with wear, a single measurement on new material may misrepresent exposure over the garment’s service life.
